summary: Ho Chi Minh City keeps the palace and the museum. Dong Hoi keeps the gate, the ruined tower, and the landing on the Nhật Lệ. Cu Chi is the tunnels.
body: The Reunification Palace is the former presidential palace, kept as it was in 1975, including the war rooms. The War Remnants Museum is a direct, photographic museum. It is distressing and crowded. Read it slowly or not at all.

In Dong Hoi, Quảng Bình Quan is the south gate of the Lũy Thầy line. The ward page dates the rampart to 1631, the rebuild to 1825, and a repair to 1961. A visitor note says 1630. Tam Toa is the ruined bell tower in the central park. The ward page says the church was built in 1886. Mother Suốt is the landing where Nguyễn Thị Suốt rowed soldiers, ammunition, and messages across the Nhật Lệ. Pac Bo, about 55 km north of Cao Bang city, is the Coc Bo walk. Cu Chi is a half-day from the city center. The visitor tunnel is a short section widened for visitors. It is still narrow, dark, and hot.
